instrument: xml claim mapping — the analyzer's OWN resolvability classes routed to the gate claim whose check can verify them
question: the gate counted 332 edges as `unresolved` on the 2,081-file `.xml` draw. The analyzer already knew what they were (`metadata.resolvable`). Which claim key can VERIFY each class, so the bucket becomes attributed rather than merely smaller?

sites: references / attribute_qname_reference — marked when the analyzer's class is `builtin` or `external`
references / entity_reference — marked when the class is `builtin` (the five predefined entities)

notMarked.references / unresolvable X13 class: no claim. The analyzer's own class says THIS FILE does not satisfy the reference; calling that `not in the population` would assert a fact the analyzer did not measure.
notMarked.imports / class `file` (relative paths,: no claim. `importProjectFile` VERIFIES when a candidate is an admitted file and REFUTES when none is; a refutation is `extFAIL`, which must stay 0. The analyzer cannot see the project's file list, so it cannot make that claim safely.
notMarked.references / xslt_named_template_referen: emit only `in-document` / `unresolved` classes — nothing external to claim.

beforeAfter.population: 2,081 `.xml` files across 51 repositories, 0 degraded, 0 parse failures — the identical draw both runs, guarded by .bb-heavy-v3.lock

before.verdict: VERDICT: FAIL — 64 ambiguous + 332 unresolved of 30676 edges

after.verdict: VERDICT: FAIL — 64 ambiguous + 123 unresolved of 30676 edges; 34 external claim(s) unverifiable (175 verified + 34 unverifiable external)

reading.references: 198 -> 15, with 175 VERIFIED externals and 8 the owner lookup cannot reach
reading.imports: 134 -> 108, all 26 of the claimed ones unverifiable — a URI is path-like and verifyExternalClaim returns externalUnverified before any owner lookup
reading.extFAIL: 0 -> 0. No claim this lane made was refuted: the control that matters.

whyThisIsClassificationAndNotLaundering.theGatesOwnRule: script/m14/incoming-gate.ts verdict(): a PASS requires bad===0 AND externalUnverified===0 AND bindingUnverified===0. Moving an edge from `unresolved` into `externalUnverified` LOWERS the residual column and still blocks a green row — the 34 unverifiable claims above are visible in the verdict line, not hidden.
whyThisIsClassificationAndNotLaundering.theClaimIsChecked: `isExternalTarget` is verified by `verifyExternalClaim` against the project's key space: an identifier-shaped target is `externalVerified` only when nothing in the project declares it, and `externalRefuted` when something does. 175 edges earned that verification here.
whyThisIsClassificationAndNotLaundering.theDirectionOfError: The rule checks `pathLikeTarget(tgt)` FIRST and returns externalUnverified for a path, so a URI or a hyphenated DTD name (`attribute-name`, `element-name`, `processing-instruction`) can never be a false refutation. This is the opposite of the failure another lane hit tonight, where a FILE's stem was asked an OWNER question and produced 103 refutations.
whyThisIsClassificationAndNotLaundering.unattributedBecomesAttributed: The objective's bar is externalRefuted = 0 AND every non-resolved edge attributed to a named cause. Before, 332 edges carried no reason at all; after, 209 of them carry a verified or unverifiable external claim and 123 remain, each of them a class the analyzer deliberately did not claim (X13 `unresolved` references, `file`-class imports).
